audits.title: 2833 Quality improvement project on increasing antimicrobial stewardship and patient safety
audits.standard: Microguide local antimicrobial guidance; indication, route, duration and choice of antibiotic
audits.setting: Six geriatric wards, Broomfield Hospital, Mid-South Essex NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 99 of 168 patients on antibiotics; Microguide compliance 39-65% (mean 53%); indication and duration on drug charts 89%.

audits.intervention: Weekly microbiology consultant-led ward rounds, education for junior doctors, nurses and consultants, streamlined IT access to Microguide, AMS meetings and prescribing in simulation sessions.

cycle2.result: Compliance 70-90% (mean 83%); indication and duration on drug charts 95%.

audits.other_findings: Co-amoxiclav (n = 45) and Tazocin (n = 14) were the most used antibiotics; co-amoxiclav for UTI and Tazocin without microbiology approval were targeted.
audits.citation: Tarkas T, Suthahar Y. 2833 Quality improvement project on increasing antimicrobial stewardship and patient safety. Age and Ageing. 2025;54(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/ageing/afae277.018.

audits.title: A Retrospective Audit of Indication and Duration Documentation in Relation to Antimicrobial Prescribing in Residential Care
audits.standard: Two HSE standards for documentation of indication and duration on antimicrobial prescriptions
audits.setting: Four extended care units for residents over 65, Our Lady's Hospice and Care Services, Dublin

cycle1.result: Of 136 antimicrobial prescriptions, 63.24% had indication, 66.18% duration and 55.88% both documented; 55/84 residents (65.5%) had at least one antimicrobial.

audits.other_findings: Oral/enteral prescriptions had highest adherence (88.90%) vs topical 49.5%; no prophylactic prescriptions (n = 32) had indication or duration recorded.
audits.citation: Wu B, McAdam C, McDonald H, O'Dwyer E. A Retrospective Audit of Indication and Duration Documentation in Relation to Antimicrobial Prescribing in Residential Care. Age and Ageing. 2025;54(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.189.

audits.title: 3663 Improving antibiotic prescribing practices: a quality improvement project
audits.standard: Antibiotic prescribing guidelines: indication, duration, end-date documentation and PPI co-prescription

cycle1.result: Guideline adherence 65%; end-date documentation 75%; unjustified PPI co-prescription 50%.

audits.intervention: Poster on prescriber responsibilities, then an educational talk.

cycle2.result: Guideline adherence 72%; end-date documentation 85%; unjustified PPI co-prescription 33%.

audits.other_findings: After the poster alone (intermediate cycle): adherence 68%, end-date documentation 84%, unjustified PPI co-prescription 43%.
audits.citation: Attolico A, Homayooni A, Nathaniel A, Jegard J. 3663 Improving antibiotic prescribing practices: a quality improvement project. Age and Ageing. 2026;55(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.010.

audits.title: 352 A Retrospective Audit to Determine the Appropriateness of Antibiotic Use in Surgical Patients in MKUH
audits.setting: Emergency Surgery Clinic, Milton Keynes University Hospital

cycle1.result: 218 (27%) given antibiotics; only 77 (35%) of these prescribed appropriately.

audits.other_findings: All UTI patients (n = 15) treated correctly; 71% of renal stone patients (n = 68) incorrectly given antibiotics.
audits.citation: Stone H, Khanna A, Keeler B. 352 A Retrospective Audit to Determine the Appropriateness of Antibiotic Use in Surgical Patients in MKUH. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab134.262.

audits.title: 71 Electronic Prescribing Promotes Antimicrobial Stewardship In Surgery: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.standard: Public Health England antimicrobial standards: documentation of allergy status, prescriber contact, indication and review/stop dates; appropriate antimicrobial choice and IV/total duration
audits.setting: West Middlesex University Hospital, surgical inpatients

cycle1.result: Prescriber contact details 69%, review/stop dates 17%, indications 78%, appropriate selection 76%, appropriate IV duration 63%, total duration 87%.

audits.intervention: Educational session, once-weekly microbiology round of surgical inpatients and introduction of electronic prescribing (Cerner).

cycle2.result: Prescriber contact details 100%, review/stop dates 100%, indications 96%, selection 90%, IV duration 93%, total duration 100%; p < 0.05 throughout.

audits.other_findings: E-prescribing prompts clinicians to enter contact details, review dates and indications before prescribing, which partly explained the improvement.
audits.citation: Lee A, Kelly M, Maden C, McHardy J, Elfadl D. 71 Electronic Prescribing Promotes Antimicrobial Stewardship In Surgery: A Closed-Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab134.359.

audits.title: EP-3 Quality improvement project analysing the impact on antimicrobial prescribing in a General Surgery department after introducing access to guidelines via a mobile phone app
audits.standard: NICE antimicrobial stewardship guideline NG15 1.1.2.4 and trust guidelines
audits.setting: General surgery department, Peterborough City Hospital

cycle1.result: 57% of antibiotic prescriptions were in line with the correct treatment guidelines (238 prescriptions from 109 patients).

audits.intervention: Trust guidelines put on the Microguide mobile app and laptops; educational posters and a presentation to the surgical department.

cycle2.result: Accuracy of antibiotic prescriptions significantly improved; no figures given.

audits.other_findings: Some improvement in documentation of indication and duration of antibiotic prescriptions.
audits.citation: Bharadwaj A, Donald N. EP-3 Quality improvement project analysing the impact on antimicrobial prescribing in a General Surgery department after introducing access to guidelines via a mobile phone app. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_5). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac245.001.

audits.title: 804 Improving Antimicrobial Stewardship in Acute Urology: A Two-Cycle Targeted Intervention Audit Using a Composite Compliance Framework
audits.standard: Local antimicrobial guidelines across four domains: initiation, changes, discharge and duration
audits.setting: Acute urology admissions, tertiary urology centre, Liverpool University Hospitals

cycle1.result: Initial antibiotic choice 59%; duration 61%; subsequent changes 86%; discharge 61%; composite compliance 43%.

audits.intervention: QR-code posters, teaching sessions and a faculty meeting.

cycle2.result: Initial choice 82%; duration 68%; subsequent changes 81%; discharge 61%; composite compliance 53% (33% compliant, 20% justified deviations, 48% unjustified deviations).

audits.other_findings: Discharge antibiotic choice stayed at 61%; length of stay differences (p=0.002) reflected illness severity rather than compliance.
audits.citation: Farag A, Kardas K, Starmer B. 804 Improving Antimicrobial Stewardship in Acute Urology: A Two-Cycle Targeted Intervention Audit Using a Composite Compliance Framework. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.250.
